measurement.note: Every outcome below was measured against PractRand 0.95 with the seed above, at the width it is recorded under. failsBy is the smallest PractRand length at which a definitive FAIL was observed; a run whose budget is under that length cannot discriminate the control and is reported as inconclusive rather than as a harness fault. cleanThrough is its mirror for a generator expected to pass: the largest length at which a clean run was actually observed. It exists because a pass is only evidence at a depth where something worse would have been caught, and scripts/tests/test-random-quality-outcomes.mjs refuses a pass recorded shallower than that width's deepest control. The two widths are nested rather than split into two entries per name because the contract test asserts host --list order and uniqueness by name. They are NOT redundant: five generators answer a 64-bit draw from one raw word, so half of it reaches a caller only through NextDouble, NextLong and NextUlong(max) and appears in no 32-bit draw at all; and for the generators that do build NextUlong from two NextUint draws the host still packs them high-word-first and writes little-endian, so the 64-bit stream is the 32-bit one with each adjacent word pair SWAPPED. SystemRandom is the proof: it fails 32-bit at exactly 8GB and is clean through 8GB at 64-bit.

32.reason: Chaotic ARX mixer; clean through 8GB with no anomalies.

64.reason: Chaotic ARX mixer; clean through 8GB with 1 anomaly line and no failure.

32.reason: Weak by rating, but not assertable as a control at any budget measured so far. It reflects into the host System.Random's internal state, so its stream is runtime-dependent by construction: the .NET 9 stream this host emits is not the Mono stream Unity ships. Measured clean through 16GB under .NET 9, so a pass is always reported as inconclusive rather than as a harness fault.

64.reason: Clean through 8GB. Same caveat as the 32-bit width: it reflects into the host System.Random, so the stream is runtime-dependent by construction and a pass is reported as inconclusive rather than as a harness fault.

64.reason: Fails by 4KB, the same depth as the 32-bit width -- a truncated LCG is linear in every word.

32.reason: Large-state ARX generator over a 1024-word ring; clean through 8GB with no anomalies.
Expected-failure control. Knuth subtractive lagged-Fibonacci; survives 4GB and fails the low-byte BCFN test at 8GB, so only budgets of 8GB or more discriminate it.

64.reason: Clean through 8GB, where the 32-bit width fails at exactly 8GB. Its NextUlong is the base implementation -- two NextUint draws packed high-word-first and written little-endian -- so this stream is the 32-bit one with each adjacent word pair SWAPPED, not the same bytes. The 32-bit failure is at the deepest block only, and the swap perturbs it away. Rated Poor, so a pass here is reported as inconclusive rather than as a harness fault.

32.reason: Expected-failure control. Single-word chaotic generator with no formal test results; fails BCFN and DC6 within the first 64KB.

64.reason: Fails by 32KB, one block EARLIER than the 32-bit width's 64KB.

32.reason: Expected-failure control. A 1024-entry lookup table of 32-bit values with period 1024 draws; the stream repeats every 4KB, so Gap-16 catches it at 8KB. Deterministic by design and not statistically random at all.

32.reason: xoroshiro128+ returning the high 32 bits; clean through 8GB with no anomalies. It was an expected-failure control while it returned the LOW half, whose bit 0 has linear complexity exactly 128 and which fails [Low1/32]BRank(12):256(1) by 16MB. Both halves of the same algorithm were measured against this battery, so this pass is paired with the failure it replaced rather than standing alone.
